ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the probability of a standard score: hop 1 forms the standard scores, documented as exactly the difference between the point and the mean divided by the standard deviation; hop 2 creates the probability array and returns it; hops 3 and 4 pass the scores and the array along. The gold's javadoc promises, for each standard score, the probability that a standard normal variable is less than it; at the score -40 the variant gold calls Erf.erf, whose series cannot converge there (Erf.erf: '@throws MathException if the algorithm fails to converge'), and throws MaxIterationsExceededException instead of writing the probability (0 to double precision). The exception escapes before any caller sees a result, so no later hop can recover the value without a try/catch and a second evaluation, and no earlier hop can keep the score from the gold in one line without breaking its documented scores. The convention that a far score has probability 0 or 1 is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc (beyond 20 standard deviations the convergence exception is caught and 0 or 1 returned), NormalDistributionImpl.getDomainLowerBound / getDomainUpperBound (the inverse's bracketing domain runs to -Double.MAX_VALUE / Double.MAX_VALUE) and AbstractContinuousDistribution.inverseCumulativeProbability (which evaluates the distribution function at those bounds when bracketing fails); testQuantiles, testCumulativeProbabilities, testInverseCumulativeProbabilities and PoissonDistributionTest.testNormalApproximateProbability pass through the chain.
